title: SDT-Navier Field Theory
description: Local field formulation of Spatial Displacement Theory, converting the master equation into field equations for spation flow and multi-body interactions.

overview.abstract: We establish the SDT-Navier field theory, converting the SDT master equation into a local field formulation suitable for numerical simulation. The field theory describes spation flow, curvature evolution, and slip dynamics on a dodecahedral/RRPT lattice. All field equations are derived from the four irreducible primitives with complete mathematical rigor. We demonstrate that the pressure field originates from CMB influx, and all forces emerge from pressure gradients. The framework is applied to light nuclear systems with predictions validated against experimental data.
keyPoints: Local field formulation of the SDT master equation
Five continuous fields: pressure, velocity, curvature density, slip field, energy density
CMB as fundamental pressure source for all fields
Validated against nuclear binding energies and magnetic moments

keyConcepts.name: SDT-Navier Field State
keyConcepts.description: Five continuous fields describing the local state: pressure P(x,t), velocity v(x,t), curvature density κ(x,t), slip field η(x,t), and energy density e(x,t).
keyConcepts.importance: Provides complete local description of spation dynamics, enabling multi-body simulations and numerical solutions.

keyConcepts.name: Local Energy Transfer
keyConcepts.description: Local energy density rate ė(x,t) = P(x,t) × σ(x,t), where σ is the diversion density combining circulation, curvature, and slip factors.
keyConcepts.importance: Converts global master equation into local field form suitable for spatial flow calculations.

keyConcepts.name: Incompressibility Constraint
keyConcepts.description: ∇·v = 0, ensuring volume conservation in the spation medium with no gaps or compressibility.
keyConcepts.importance: Fundamental constraint from spation properties, enabling stable numerical solutions.

keyConcepts.name: Spation Flow Dynamics
keyConcepts.description: Momentum conservation equation: ρ_s(Dv/Dt) = -∇P - α∇κ - βηv, where curvature and slip forces drive flow.
keyConcepts.importance: Describes how pressure gradients and geometric factors control spation movement.

keyConcepts.name: Curvature Evolution
keyConcepts.description: Dκ/Dt = C(κ,v) - D(κ,η), where creation from converging flow balances destruction from slip.
keyConcepts.importance: Explains how toroidal structures form and maintain stable curvature through dynamic balance.

keyConcepts.name: Slip Dynamics
keyConcepts.description: Dη/Dt = S_strain(κ,v) - S_healing(κ), where strain increases slip but stable curvature reduces it.
keyConcepts.importance: Controls coupling efficiency between matter and spation, affecting energy transfer rates.

keyConcepts.name: CMB Pressure Source
keyConcepts.description: P(x,t) = ∫ I_CMB(î)[1 - E(x,î,t)] dΩ, where CMB radiation continuously maintains pressure fields.
keyConcepts.importance: Links microscopic field theory to cosmological energy source, eliminating infinite energy densities.

derivations.description: Local energy density evolution from pressure and diversion density.
steps: Global master equation: Ė = P_∞ A_eff Γ κ (1-η)
Convert to local form: ė = P × σ

derivations.name: Spation Flow Equation
derivations.description: Momentum conservation in spation medium with curvature and slip forces.

derivations.name: CMB Pressure Field
derivations.description: Pressure field from CMB radiation, reduced by matter occlusion.
steps: CMB intensity I_CMB(î) from direction î
Matter creates deficits: ΔP = -∫ I_CMB E dΩ

derivations.name: Deuteron Binding Energy
derivations.description: Nuclear binding from reduced slip in bound systems.
steps: Free nucleons have higher slip η_free
Bound system reduces slip to η_bound
Binding energy = P_CMB A_eff Γ κ (η_free - η_bound)
Slip reduction enables stable nuclear binding
